s.g: Used to form adjectives from verbs, especially those in -ать (-atʹ).
Combining form used to form prefixed perfective verbs, with the approximate meaning "to turn".
Whatman paper, wove paper (high-quality drawing paper)
to rise in price, to go up
Harrisburg (the capital city of Pennsylvania, United States)
game (wild animals or birds hunted for food)
to tire out, to overwork, to underfeed, to give short rations
as such, by itself, by oneself, per se, individually
punch, center punch (device for creating holes in thin material)
to tack (to turn the bow through the wind)
chanterelle (a mushroom of the Cantharellus genus)
mistress (female extramarital lover, often financially supported)
to sniff around, to sniff on all sides
to stun (especially with a heavy blow)
to examine, to inspect, to look over (once)
to get out of the habit (of), to break oneself of the habit (of)
to grind, to polish, to file
pattern (intelligible arrangement which has a mathematical, geometric, statistical etc. relationship)
national (a person owing allegiance to a state)
citizen (a person who possesses citizenship of a state)
to hook on, to pick up
to argue, to fight (for a while)
to equate, to put/place on the same footing, to give the same status
hedonism (a general devotion to the pursuit of pleasure)
epithalamium (poetic work in the nature of a panegyric on the occasion of a wedding)
